{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVaC1p88AAAABayDlmQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BpEKozhEYDMI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BpEKo", "number": 14, "title": "Add a CPU bus and ROM/RAM test harness for browser RTL simulation", "body": "## Problem

WebRTL can compile multi-file Verilog projects in the browser (#12) and has reusable output interfaces (#10), but it has no small, tested example of a CPU-style memory bus connected to ROM and RAM. This is the next prerequisite before integrating an SNES 65C816 RTL core. The implementation should remain useful for other CPU and computer designs.

## Expected outcome

Provide a **generic synthesizable CPU-bus and ROM/RAM test harness** that compiles and runs entirely in the existing GitHub Pages browser workflow.

A small **test bus master** (not a 65C816 implementation) should issue reads and writes through a documented bus interface, fetch known bytes from a tiny ROM, store/read data in RAM, and expose observable results. The example should work across separate Verilog files with a selectable top module.

## Scope

- Define a minimal synchronous CPU/memory bus contract: clock/reset, address, read/write direction or enables, write data, read data, and transaction timing. Choose and document the initial address/data widths and any ready/wait behavior; keep the interface suitable for later adaptation to a 65C816 core without claiming SNES-specific timing.
- Implement a small synthesizable ROM, initialized from inline test data (no browser-side HDL `$readmemh` dependency), and a writable RAM with a documented address map.
- Add address decoding and a tiny RTL test bus master/state machine that demonstrates ROM reads, RAM writes, and RAM readback, including reset behavior.
- Integrate a minimal **observable output** in the current WebRTL browser simulation (such as a named test-result/status register using the existing supported output adapter, or a small focused adapter if necessary). Do not build a full general-purpose CPU debugger or arbitrary pin/port framework.
- Include a multi-file example selectable from the existing project UI. Keep the counter, video and audio examples working.
- Document the bus timing, memory map, expected read/write sequence and how to run and inspect the test.

## Out of scope

- Implementing, importing or verifying a real 65C816 CPU core.
- Full SNES memory mapping, DMA, PPU, APU, cartridge mappers, or real game ROMs.
- Large ROM upload tools, memory initialization from arbitrary external files, a generic peripheral framework, or full IDE/debugger expansion.
- Physical FPGA integration or cycle-accurate SNES bus timing.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Multiple Verilog files describing the bus master, ROM, RAM, decoder and top-level harness can be compiled into WASM **entirely in the browser**, served from the static `/webrtl/` path.
- [ ] An automated browser test observes the circuit read known test bytes from ROM, write them (or documented transformations) to RAM, and read back expected results. The observed values must originate from compiled RTL, not from a JavaScript reimplementation.
- [ ] The output exposes an unambiguous pass/fail or traceable result so the sequence can be validated without manual or physical-device confirmation.
- [ ] Reset is deterministic and repeated runs/steps give consistent results; invalid/incompatible design changes produce actionable compilation errors.
- [ ] The existing counter, multi-file, video and audio browser functionality remains operational (appropriate regression tests).
- [ ] The bus signals, timing assumptions, address map, sample program/data and limits are documented; no claims of full 65C816/SNES compatibility.
- [ ] The work is focused on the test harness, not speculative CPU-debugging infrastructure.

## Optional validation

- Report simulated cycles/second for the test harness.
- Evaluate how an actual 65C816 RTL core might connect to this bus as a follow-up, without requiring core integration now.

## Required post-merge verification

After deployment, verify through an automated browser run that the public GitHub Pages example completes its ROM-to-RAM sequence and reports the expected result. This live check is separate from pre-merge acceptance.

## Related

- #3 — WebRTL project vision
- #12 — Multi-file RTL project support
- #10 — Video/audio interfaces
- Follow-up: integrate a real 65C816 RTL core with a tiny permitted test ROM.
